## Why
`merge_works()` returns oeuvre candidates sorted by `(year, title)` so discovery UIs present chronologically sensible lists. At `src/fine_art_archive/known_works/fetchers.py:338` the sort key uses `w.year or 9999`, so astronomical year `0` (1 BCE) is treated as missing and sorted after modern works instead of before year `1`. The playlist artist sort bug filed as #714 fixed the same falsiness pattern in `eink/playlist.py`, but this path was left unchanged.

Verified on tip `5fb9a7d`: `merge_works([KnownWork(title='Year zero', year=0)], [KnownWork(title='Year one', year=1)])` returns titles `['Year one', 'Year zero']` instead of year-zero first.

## Scope
- `src/fine_art_archive/known_works/fetchers.py`
- `tests/test_known_works_fetchers.py`

## Non-Goals
- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: adding a comment without changing the sort key is a failure of this issue.
- Do NOT change merge deduplication keys or `display_score` weighting in the same edit.

## Tasks
- [ ] At `src/fine_art_archive/known_works/fetchers.py:338`, replace `w.year or 9999` with `w.year if w.year is not None else 9999` so year `0` sorts before positive years.
- [ ] Add `test_merge_works_sorts_astronomical_year_zero_before_year_one` in `tests/test_known_works_fetchers.py` asserting merged order `['Year zero', 'Year one', 'Unknown year']` for year `0`, year `1`, and `year=None` works.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `pytest tests/test_known_works_fetchers.py -k merge_works_sorts_astronomical_year_zero` passes.
- Deliberate break: restore `w.year or 9999` at `src/fine_art_archive/known_works/fetchers.py:338`, run the named pytest, and verify it FAILS; revert to pass.

_Surfaced by Track D repo-audit 2026-09-23; verified by executing `merge_works` on tip `5fb9a7d`._
title: [P2] merge_works sorts astronomical year 0 as missing year (fetchers.py:338)
